description: What a verifier of a composite signature MUST refuse, and why. The companion to composite-m-prime: that vector fixes the message, this one fixes the decisions taken around it.
why_this_is_a_primitive: A valid signature proves the maths works; it says nothing about what an implementation does with an INVALID one. The refusals below are policy the code enforces, not properties the cryptography provides — most notably the post-quantum floor, whose absence leaves a composite whose remaining half verifies perfectly. Two implementations that disagree here disagree about which certificates exist, and no positive test on either side notices.
not_a_cryptographic_soundness_test: This does not attempt to show that no forged signature ever verifies. That is a property of ECDSA and ML-DSA, provided by whatever library an implementation links, and it is not something a fixture can establish. What is pinned here is the finite, enumerable set of decisions the CALLING code makes before and after it asks the library anything.
payload_note: The digest is SHA3-256(JCS(signed view)) of the independence-proof golden, so the valid case is a signature produced by the reference producer implementation with test keys (hedged, so verified rather than reproduced) rather than a synthesized one. The mutated cases derive from it by changing exactly one thing each.
verification_rule: verify(composite_alg_id, payload_canon_digest_hex, signature, keys) succeeds iff: the signature object carries exactly alg, mode and signatures; its alg equals the expected profile and its mode is AND; signatures holds exactly the profile's components in the profile's order (classical first, ML-DSA-65 second), each with exactly its members — the ECDSA one with encoding "raw-rs-64" and low_s true; the classical key is in the one encoding its profile fixes (P-256: 65-byte SEC1 uncompressed; Ed25519: raw 32 bytes) and the ML-DSA-65 key is 1952 bytes; and every component verifies over M' = the framing in composite-m-prime. A case's classical_public_key_b64, when present, replaces the pinned classical key for that case. Any other outcome is a refusal.

cases.label: valid
cases.why: the unmodified composite: both components verify against M' under the pinned keys

cases.label: missing-mldsa-component
cases.why: THE case this vector exists for. The classical component still verifies perfectly, so an implementation that treats the post-quantum half as optional accepts this and every cryptographic check it runs passes. The PQC floor is a POLICY the code enforces, not a property the maths provides — nothing else catches its absence

cases.label: missing-classical-component
cases.why: AND means both; a composite carrying one half is not a weaker composite, it is not one

cases.label: profile-mismatch
cases.why: the signature declares one profile and the caller expects another. The profile is framed into M', so this must be refused before any component is checked — see composite-m-prime

cases.label: mode-not-and
cases.why: OR would let either half alone carry the signature, which is exactly what the composite exists to prevent. Unknown modes are refused rather than interpreted

cases.label: unknown-classical-alg
cases.why: an algorithm the verifier does not implement is refused, never skipped: skipping it would silently reduce the composite to its post-quantum half

cases.label: tampered-classical-signature
cases.why: one flipped bit in the classical component. The ML-DSA half still verifies, so an implementation that stops at the first success accepts it

cases.label: tampered-mldsa-signature
cases.why: the mirror case: the classical half verifies and the post-quantum one does not

cases.label: components-reordered
cases.why: both components are present and each verifies over M', but the PQC one comes first. The order is normative (composite-signature/1 §7, §8): an implementation that searches the array instead of reading it in order accepts this, and two byte forms of one signature then both verify

cases.label: extra-component
cases.why: a third component, a copy of the ML-DSA one. The profile fixes exactly two; tolerating a repeat or an unknown extra lets the object grow without changing what verifies

cases.label: ecdsa-encoding-not-raw-rs-64
cases.why: the ECDSA component declares encoding "der" over the same raw-rs-64 bytes. The field is fixed to "raw-rs-64" (composite-signature/1 §9.1); a verifier that ignores it accepts a declaration it does not honour

cases.label: ecdsa-low-s-false
cases.why: the ECDSA component is a valid low-s signature but declares low_s: false. The field is fixed to true (composite-signature/1 §9.1)

cases.label: ecdsa-low-s-absent
cases.why: the ECDSA component omits low_s. The component carries exactly alg, encoding, low_s and sig_b64 (composite-signature/1 §8)

cases.label: component-extra-member
cases.why: the ML-DSA component carries a member the profile does not define. Components have closed member sets (composite-signature/1 §8)

cases.label: signature-extra-member
cases.why: the composite object carries a member beyond alg, mode and signatures. With no carrying artifact defining more, the object is exactly those three (composite-signature/1 §8)

cases.label: p256-key-compressed
cases.why: the valid signature, verified under the same P-256 key compressed to 33 bytes. Every P-256 key field of the corpus admits only the 65-byte SEC1 uncompressed encoding (composite-signature/1 §9.1); accepting two encodings of one key gives every digest over it two values

cases.label: p256-key-spki
cases.why: the same key as an SPKI DER structure. Another encoding of the same key, refused for the same reason

cases.label: ed25519-raw-key-under-p256-profile
cases.why: a raw 32-byte key, the Ed25519 encoding, offered as the classical key of the canonical profile — as a capacity Level-1 key might be. The canonical profile has no Ed25519 field, so the key is malformed before any verification

must_hold: the valid case verifies, and every other case is refused
a composite with no ML-DSA-65 component is refused even though its classical half verifies
a profile mismatch is refused before any component is checked
an unrecognized component algorithm is refused, never skipped
a single tampered component fails the whole composite, whichever half it is
a composite whose components are out of the profile's order, repeated, or carry undefined members is refused even though each component verifies
a key in any encoding other than the one its field fixes is refused, even when it encodes the same key
